chapter: New York 1936-39 (second pass of the transcript)
title: Early 52nd Street and the Famous Door (second pass)
summary: Repeat of Black musicians staying uptown and the Teddy Wilson band's notice at the Famous Door.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Working the street and Louis Freeman was working in Jimmy Ryans' and Eddie Condon was working at Gallagher's and that was strictly a white --
Yeah, right, the beginning of 52nd Street was a white thing.

Right. So, with Teddy Wilson's big band, we opened at the Famous Door at January, May, in May '39, and the band was too cool for what they expected and we started out with a notice. And they wanted to get rid of us right away.

Yeah. Then after a week or so, they realized that we were a pretty good band but they had already booked Charlie Barnet to follow us, so that was the end of our 52nd Street career. But then, by the same token, John Kirby just opened at the Onyx Club, Stuff Smith. Stuff Smith had opened the Onyx Club and then, John Kirby. This is pre-war, World War II.
But up until then you were above
Other than Arcadia Ballroom where Fletcher and Roy had a big band.
